presets.name: Classic rock pedal wah
presets.desc: The standard Cry Baby voice on the expression pedal: vocal heel-to-toe sweep for rock leads

refs.why: Slash's stock Cry Baby on the Appetite-era solos

presets.notes: golem's wah block voice (GCB-95, 408 Hz to 2.25 kHz); a little resonance clipping for realism; EXP on wah

presets.name: High-gain lead wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby before a high-gain amp, slightly lower Q and a level push: screaming, cutting metal leads

refs.why: Hammett's Cry Baby lead break cutting over the riff
signature Cry Baby wah in his Black Label Society rig

presets.notes: The crate's high-gain start: Q 80 tames fizz into the amp, +3 dB hits the preamp harder; auto-engage so the foot only rocks

presets.name: Dark, wide grunge wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby with a wider sweep and a toe stop short of the top: dark, squashed wah on heavy riffs

refs.why: Cantrell's dark, punchy wah woven through the riffs

presets.notes: Range 120 widens the sweep downward; toe 85 keeps the top dark (the idea of a toe-trim pot)

presets.name: Parked-wah honk
presets.desc: Wah parked just past the middle: a fixed, nasal mid-boost that makes a driven amp snarl

refs.why: Mick Ronson's parked wah for a honking, aggressive lead tone
Brian May's wah used in fixed positions as a tone filter
Knopfler's riff through a partly-open, fixed wah

presets.notes: No EXP needed: the crate's parked-wah use (0.4 to 0.6); move wah to taste for more nasal (lower) or more cutting (higher)

presets.name: Boosted solo wah
presets.desc: Cry Baby with extra Q and a solo-level boost: the wah also lifts the lead over the band
presets.notes: Volume +5 dB covers a 535Q-style boost: engaging the wah (auto-engage) is also the solo boost

presets.name: Switchless short-throw wah
presets.desc: Turns on when the pedal moves, off when parked at heel; shorter travel with an S taper
presets.notes: Crate's switchless and smaller-travel uses together: heel 10 / toe 85 avoid the extreme mud and shriek

presets.name: Late-60s British wah
presets.desc: The original Italian-style wah voice: smooth, vocal sweep for psychedelic blues leads

refs.why: Clapton named a Vox wah for the song's wah parts
the scratched, muted wah intro and wah-soaked leads

presets.notes: Vox V847 with its own linear pot law (heel = low, fixed in this crate); drive 25 lets the peak clip into a fuzz

presets.name: Funk wacka rhythm
presets.desc: Narrow, peaky wah for muted 16th-note scratching: the 'wacka-wacka' chika rhythm

refs.why: Skip Pitts' rhythmic wah-wah guitar intro

presets.notes: Crate's funk start: Classic voice with Q 150 makes each rock of the foot a sharp vowel; rock in time with the 16ths

presets.name: Vocal, throaty lead wah
presets.desc: Wide-range, moderately peaky wah voice: a throaty, talking sweep for expressive blues leads
presets.notes: Clyde voicing (369 Hz to 2.37 kHz, Q 4.17 per Fractal) sweeps wider than the Cry Baby: more 'vowel' per inch

presets.name: Fuzzy British wah
presets.desc: Sharp, aggressive vintage wah voice driven into clipping: snarling fuzz-wah for psych and stoner
presets.notes: Colorsound keeps its inverted log pot law; drive 45 clips the resonance into a fuzz of its own

presets.name: Sixties beat-group wah
presets.desc: Gentle, lower-Q vintage British wah voice: a soft, round sweep for crunchy 60s rhythm
presets.notes: Selmer voicing with its linear pot law; Q 90 softens it further

presets.name: Bass wah, lows kept
presets.desc: Bass-voiced wah blended with the dry: a talking sweep on the mids while the low end stays put

refs.why: Cliff Burton's distorted bass solo through a wah

presets.notes: Crate's bass start: Bass 105Q voicing with mix 70 so the fundamental never disappears

presets.name: Hands-free envelope wah
presets.desc: The wah voice swept by picking dynamics instead of the foot: quacks on each attack
presets.notes: Crate's auto-wah-without-a-pedal use; for a dedicated envelope filter prefer gfx-autowah

presets.name: Rhythmic LFO wah sweep
presets.desc: An LFO rocks the wah on its own at about two sweeps a second: a cycling, psychedelic wah
presets.notes: freq is the alien LFO in BPM (120 = 2 Hz), free-running, not host-synced: set it near the song tempo

presets.name: Keys funk pedal wah
presets.desc: Round, mid-focused wah on clavinet or electric piano, swept by the foot for funky comping
presets.notes: No drive on keys; mix 85 keeps a little dry so low notes of the clav stay full
